newsitem.title: SINGAPORE: Singapore shares open higher, boosted by Dow.
newsitem.headline: Singapore shares open higher, boosted by Dow.

text.p: Singapore shares opened firmer on Tuesday, buoyed by another strong close on Wall Street.
"The market is looking up and people are now saying they may have seen the low for the year," said a dealer with a Singapore brokerage.
Index-linked stocks like Keppel Corp, Wing Tai and Singapore Telecom were among the gainers in active volumes.
At 0225 GMT, the Straits Times Industrial index was 35.12 points higher at 2,063.72. Total market volume was 47.3 million shares with 205 gainers overwhelming 18 losers.
HongKong Land Holdings rose 6.31 percent, or 14 cents, to US$2.36 in active trading after the company said it would implement a share repurchase programme.
Uraco shares touched a new 1997 low of S$0.84 before recovering to S$0.87, down one cent. Uraco has a stake in CAM International, whose auditors have accused two directors of fraud.
CAM said before the details were released it was not aware of any fraud.
Early gainers included Creative, up S$1.10 to S$23.30. Fraser & Neave and DBS foreign each rose 50 cents to S$11.40 and $18.40 respectively.
